reason: Researched via web search this week. The refiner group fell 7-8% in one session around 10-27/10-28 (MPC -7%, VLO -8%, PSX -7%, DINO -7%) with no company news, purely on signs of better U.S.-Iran relations; that move stopped out our VLO leg at -10.6%. On 10-29 Brent was still ~$115 (CNBC) after VP Vance's letter to Iran's SNSC tried to revive stalled talks, and UBS noted the talks have produced nothing substantive and sees Brent near $110 at year-end. Fundamentals have not cracked: PSX reported a record Q3 on 10-28 ($5.6B earnings, $38/bbl realized margin vs $24 in Q2, 98% utilization, record 41% distillate yield). Gulf refineries remain damaged, product flows through Hormuz are about half their prewar share, and analysts do not expect full recovery until well into 2027, so even a deal would compress crude faster than it ends the diesel shortage. MPC trades at ~6x forward earnings against an ~11.7x five-year average. The book is already sized for exactly this headline risk: only ~27% effective gross (MPC 15, PSX 12) with ~73% cash earning 4%, and MPC/PSX keep their -10% stops from the 10-19 entry fills (MPC stop ~426, about 4% below the 444.73 mark; PSX ~261.5), so a confirmed deal is capped at roughly a 1.5-2% NAV hit. I am not adding back VLO: diplomatic momentum is the near-term driver, and buying the name that just stopped out would be chasing. I am not cutting either: MPC reports ~11-03, the day after entry, and the group has already de-rated on peak-margin fears. Re-registering would only pay frictions and reset stop bases. Holding is the cheapest way to keep the refiner thesis with defined downside.
